articles.title: Supreme Court urged to leave in place order blocking construction of White House ballroom
articles.summary: The National Trust for Historic Preservation asked the Supreme Court to uphold a federal court order temporarily blocking construction of a new White House ballroom. The Trump administration was accused of rushing construction to make judicial review moot by making the project too far along to reverse.
articles.author: Amy Howe

articles.title: The chief justice should share much of his power
articles.summary: An opinion piece argues that the Chief Justice should delegate some of his traditional powers—such as presiding over oral arguments and private conferences—to other justices. The author contends this would build trust among the justices and allow experimentation with different leadership styles, and that such a change would be constitutional.
articles.author: Josh Blackman

articles.title: What if one vote had changed in the birthright citizenship case?
articles.summary: The article analyzes the Supreme Court's decision in Trump v. Barbara, which struck down an executive order attempting to end birthright citizenship for children of undocumented immigrants and temporary residents as unconstitutional under the 14th Amendment's citizenship clause. The 5-justice majority opinion was written by Chief Justice Roberts, with Justice Kavanaugh dissenting in part, and the article explores what might have changed if one vote had gone differently.
articles.author: Joshua R. Averbach, Roy T. Englert, Jr.

articles.title: Trump v. Carroll and the Ten Commandments
articles.summary: This article discusses the Trump v. Carroll case alongside Ten Commandments-related legal issues, and also touches on the national security arguments raised in the White House ballroom construction dispute before the Supreme Court.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Blake Fox

articles.title: Ballroom opponents ask Supreme Court to keep Trump project on hold
articles.summary: Opponents of the White House ballroom construction project asked the Supreme Court to keep the project on hold, after an appeals court ordered the Trump administration to halt construction by Friday. The National Trust for Historic Preservation urged the high court to allow the pause to take effect.
articles.author: Dan Diamond, Jonathan Edwards, Justin Jouvenal

articles.title: Texas families ask Supreme Court to take up challenge to Ten Commandments in schools
articles.summary: A group of Texas families has asked the Supreme Court to review a Fifth Circuit ruling that upheld a 2025 Texas law requiring the Ten Commandments to be displayed in every public school classroom. The challengers argue that the lower court disregarded binding Supreme Court precedents on the separation of church and state.
articles.author: Amy Howe

articles.title: Court turns down Trump’s request to reconsider its refusal to hear Carroll suit against him
articles.summary: The Supreme Court denied President Trump's petition for rehearing in Trump v. Carroll, a civil suit brought by journalist E. Jean Carroll that resulted in a $5 million verdict against him. The decision, issued as part of a summer orders list, came without any explanation, consistent with the Court's usual practice.
articles.author: Amy Howe

articles.title: SCOTUS litigator Floyd Abrams at 90
articles.summary: SCOTUSblog published a profile of Floyd Abrams, the renowned First Amendment litigator, on the occasion of his 90th birthday. The article highlights his career dedicated to freedom of speech and press and his enduring influence on constitutional law, rather than addressing any specific Supreme Court case.
articles.author: Ronald Collins

articles.title: Who is Justice Barrett?
articles.summary: The article examines Justice Amy Coney Barrett's judicial identity, noting that her dissents at the end of the 2024 term — including in Ohio v. EPA and Fischer v. United States — complicated the standard portrayal of her as a straightforward conservative. It explores how she has occasionally aligned with the Court's liberal justices on significant issues.
articles.author: Adam Feldman

articles.title: Emergency docket heats up
articles.summary: The article discusses the increasing activity on the Supreme Court's emergency docket and provides a refresher on the Court's lottery system for obtaining oral argument tickets. It does not focus on a specific named case from the current term.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Nora Collins

articles.title: Supreme Court Again Rejects Trump’s Appeal of $5 Million E. Jean Carroll Payment
articles.summary: The Supreme Court rejected President Trump's long-shot request to reconsider its earlier denial of his appeal in the E. Jean Carroll case, which resulted in a $5 million judgment against him. Trump has separately asked the Court to overturn a larger 2024 damages award in a related proceeding.
articles.author: Ann E. Marimow

articles.title: Supreme Court asked to hear case on Texas law requiring Ten Commandments in schools
articles.summary: Texas families have petitioned the Supreme Court to hear their challenge to a Texas law mandating the display of the Ten Commandments in public school classrooms. The case could become a landmark dispute over the constitutional separation of church and state.
articles.author: Justin Jouvenal, Laura Meckler

articles.title: Supreme Court rebuffs Trump’s bid to overturn $5 million verdict in Carroll case
articles.summary: The Supreme Court turned down President Trump's effort to overturn the $5 million verdict in the E. Jean Carroll sexual abuse and defamation case. The denial of rehearing closes one avenue of appeal, though a separate, larger damages award remains under challenge.
articles.author: Justin Jouvenal

articles.title: Hakeem Jeffries says he wants to see ‘dramatic reform’ of Supreme Court
articles.summary: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries publicly called for "dramatic reform" of the Supreme Court, signaling support for aggressive structural changes to the institution. The article focuses on political advocacy rather than any specific pending case.
articles.author: Matthew Choi

articles.title: Angry at the Supreme Court, liberals push a slew of plans for overhauling it
articles.summary: As the midterm elections approach, liberal Democrats are pushing multiple proposals to overhaul the Supreme Court, including court expansion by adding more justices, imposing term limits, and other structural reforms. The push is fueled by growing frustration among progressives with the Court's recent rulings and its conservative majority.
articles.author: Julian Mark

articles.title: Trump brings ballroom dispute to the Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Trump administration asked the Supreme Court to allow construction of a new White House ballroom to proceed while legal challenges continue in lower courts. A federal appeals court in Washington had upheld a district court order temporarily blocking the construction, but gave the government 14 days to seek Supreme Court intervention.
articles.author: Amy Howe

articles.title: Understanding the court’s next major case on asylum seekers: Wassily v. Blanche
articles.summary: The Supreme Court will hear Wassily v. Blanche, a case deciding whether asylum beneficiaries are barred from obtaining lawful permanent residency if their asylum status has been terminated. The case has gained significance due to Trump administration policy changes that have exposed more immigrants to the risk of asylum termination, and the legal question has divided federal courts.
articles.author: Duncan Fulton

articles.title: Who exactly are the “friends of the court”?
articles.summary: The Supreme Court will hear oral argument on October 13 in Beaird v. United States, a case involving a Texas man challenging a sentence enhancement for possessing a gun after a prior felony conviction. The case is notable because the federal government itself is urging the Court to overturn the Fifth Circuit ruling that upheld the sentence, creating the need for outside 'friends of the court' to defend the lower court's decision.
articles.author: Amy Howe

articles.title: The transformation of Supreme Court arguments
articles.summary: This article discusses how Supreme Court oral arguments have evolved over time, alongside news that a top Democratic leader is calling for Supreme Court reform. The piece examines changes in how justices engage with lawyers during arguments and broader institutional changes at the Court.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Nora Collins

articles.title: Trump Administration Asks Supreme Court to Greenlight White House Ballroom
articles.summary: The Trump administration asked the Supreme Court to allow construction of a planned 90,000-square-foot White House ballroom, estimated to cost $400 million, to move forward. The project is part of the president's broader effort to reshape Washington, and the legal fight has now escalated to the nation's highest court after lower courts blocked construction.
articles.author: Ann E. Marimow

articles.title: An Unlikely Emergency Appeal to the Supreme Court From a Dog Named Bruce
articles.summary: An emergency appeal was filed with the Supreme Court on behalf of a dog named Bruce that a judge found to be "vicious," highlighting the growing use of the Court's emergency docket. The case illustrates how the shadow docket has expanded to include increasingly unusual last-ditch filings seeking immediate Supreme Court intervention.
articles.author: Ann E. Marimow

articles.title: Trump officials ask Supreme Court to let ballroom construction continue
articles.summary: Trump administration officials asked the Supreme Court to permit continued construction of a controversial White House ballroom project, escalating the legal dispute to the highest court. Lower courts had temporarily blocked the construction, and the administration is seeking to overturn those rulings.
articles.author: Jonathan Edwards, Justin Jouvenal, Dan Diamond

articles.title: Once upon a time: storytelling in Learning Resources v. Trump
articles.summary: This article uses the Supreme Court case Learning Resources v. Trump as a teaching example for legal writing, focusing on storytelling techniques in legal briefs. It discusses how good writing principles, rather than just avoiding bad legal writing habits, can improve advocacy before the Court.
articles.author: Kendall Gray

articles.title: The Supreme Court expands protections for digital data – now what?
articles.summary: The article analyzes the Supreme Court's decision in Chatrie v. United States, which established that digital location data is protected under the Fourth Amendment and requires a warrant for police searches. The piece explores how the ruling could lead to a broader expansion of digital privacy protections beyond the specific facts of the case.
articles.author: Mailyn Fidler

articles.title: Trump administration asks SCOTUS to rule soon on mail-in voting
articles.summary: The Trump administration has asked the Supreme Court to expedite a ruling on a case involving mail-in voting. The article also touches on whether Republicans are becoming less supportive of the Supreme Court.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas

articles.title: After Supreme Court Losses, Trump Keeps Pushing
articles.summary: The article examines the Trump administration's response to multiple losses at the Supreme Court, questioning whether the administration is defying court rulings or pursuing lawful alternative strategies to achieve its policy goals.
articles.author: Adam Liptak

articles.title: How Supreme Court Oral Arguments Have Transformed Since Covid-Era Precautions
articles.summary: The article explores how Supreme Court oral arguments have been transformed since Covid-era changes, including the introduction of live audio broadcasts and a new questioning format. These procedural shifts have given new voices prominence and altered the Court's most important public-facing tradition.
articles.author: Adam Liptak

articles.title: Trump administration urges Supreme Court to issue a decision in mail-in voting dispute
articles.summary: The Trump administration is urging the Supreme Court to act quickly on its pending request to block a federal judge's ruling that prevents implementation of part of an executive order on mail-in voting in 23 states and D.C. ahead of November elections. Solicitor General Sauer emphasized the urgency of the matter, which was filed on July 27 and has been fully briefed.
articles.author: Amy Howe

articles.title: SCOTUS has issued its decisions. Now Congress has the floor.
articles.summary: An opinion piece argues that Congress should respond constructively to Supreme Court statutory interpretation decisions rather than resorting to partisan attacks. The article criticizes the current dynamic where Congress accuses the court of being too political rather than using its legislative power to amend statutes it believes were misinterpreted.
articles.author: James Valvo , Cindy Crawford

articles.title: Are Republicans falling out of love with the Supreme Court?
articles.summary: Recent public opinion polls show a significant partisan divide in views of the Supreme Court, with 74% of Republicans approving of the court compared to just 22% of Democrats. The article examines whether Republican support for the court may be starting to erode, noting Democrats are more likely to say the court has too much power or has given the president too much authority.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas

articles.title: The new birthright citizenship battle
articles.summary: The Supreme Court is facing a new legal battle over birthright citizenship. Additionally, the court has scheduled seven cases for its November argument session, signaling a busy upcoming term.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Nora Collins

articles.title: Are Republicans Falling Out of Love With the Supreme Court?
articles.summary: An article explores whether Republican support for the Supreme Court is declining, with Justice Amy Coney Barrett receiving the most criticism from GOP members. The piece examines the shifting dynamics of conservative attitudes toward the court they helped shape through judicial appointments.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas

articles.title: Challenge brought to Trump’s new birthright citizenship order
articles.summary: Plaintiffs who previously won a challenge to President Trump's first executive order restricting birthright citizenship have returned to federal court in New Hampshire to challenge a new, revised executive order on the same topic. The ACLU and other civil rights organizations filed a motion shortly after Trump signed the new order, which again seeks to narrow automatic citizenship for babies born in the United States.
articles.author: Amy Howe

articles.title: Court announces cases it will hear in November, including religious discrimination dispute
articles.summary: The Supreme Court released its November argument calendar, announcing it will hear seven hours of oral arguments over five days. Among the cases are a dispute involving a Catholic preschool's challenge to its exclusion from a Colorado preschool program on religious discrimination grounds, and a case about an inmate's ability to sue a federal prison official for constitutional rights violations.
articles.author: Amy Howe

articles.title: The court should hold oral argument outside of the capital
articles.summary: An opinion piece argues that the Supreme Court should hold oral arguments outside of Washington, D.C. The article traces the Court's history of different locations and notes the precedent set during the pandemic when the Court adapted its proceedings, suggesting the justices could benefit from engaging with the public beyond the capital.
articles.author: Josh Blackman

articles.title: Weakening the protection against sex discrimination?
articles.summary: An analysis piece examines the Supreme Court's ruling in West Virginia v. B.P.J., which upheld a West Virginia law barring transgender girls and women from participating in sports matching their gender identity. The article argues that while the outcome was expected, the Court's reasoning—analyzing the law as sex discrimination under equal protection rather than gender identity discrimination—could have troubling implications for broader sex discrimination protections.
articles.author: Erwin Chemerinsky

articles.title: A reflection on John Roberts
articles.summary: A reflective piece looks back on Chief Justice John Roberts's tenure and legacy on the Supreme Court. The article also discusses the historical aftermath of Homer Plessy's life following the landmark Plessy v. Ferguson decision.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Blake Fox

articles.title: Trump refuses to back down as Supreme Court blocks major policies
articles.summary: President Trump is seeking ways to work around several Supreme Court rulings that blocked major administration policies, including those on tariffs, birthright citizenship, and the Federal Reserve. Experts say that while Trump's moves don't constitute outright defiance of the Court, they push the boundaries of the Court's authority and test its limits.
articles.author: Julian Mark

articles.title: SCOTUS’s October Preview
articles.summary: A preview article looks ahead to the Supreme Court's upcoming October session and the cases the justices will consider. The piece also touches on the return of the birthright citizenship issue to the legal spotlight following renewed executive action by the Trump administration.
articles.author: Zachary Shemtob, Amy Howe

articles.title: The Supreme Court and the Indian nations
articles.summary: This article, adapted from a forthcoming essay collection, examines the legal and historical relationship between the Supreme Court and Indian nations. It discusses how Native Americans were characterized in founding documents and how Supreme Court jurisprudence has shaped federal Indian law over the centuries.
articles.author: Joseph William Singer

articles.title: 12 angry men – or six?
articles.summary: The Supreme Court will hear Kian v. Florida in its upcoming term, a case challenging whether the Constitution requires 12-person juries for serious criminal cases or whether states like Florida can use juries of only six. The article revisits the Court's earlier ruling in Williams v. Florida, which had allowed smaller juries, and explores whether the Court may now reconsider that precedent.
articles.author: Anastasia Boden

articles.title: Justice Alito isn’t going anywhere
articles.summary: The article reports that Justice Samuel Alito has no plans to retire from the Supreme Court, despite speculation. It also notes that a legal dispute over the use of the White House ballroom is likely to reach the Supreme Court.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Eli Kronenberg

articles.title: The Delusions of John Roberts
articles.summary: The article critiques Chief Justice John Roberts for publicly maintaining that the Supreme Court is impartial and non-partisan, while arguing that the Court's recent decisions reflect a consistent and dramatic shift to the right. It examines the tension between Roberts's rhetoric about judicial neutrality and the Court's substantive rulings.
articles.author: Margaret Talbot

articles.title: Trump Officials Under Pressure to Deport Haitians After Supreme Court Win on T.P.S. Program
articles.summary: Following the Supreme Court's ruling in favor of the Trump administration regarding the Temporary Protected Status (TPS) program, Trump officials are facing pressure from supporters to aggressively carry out deportations of Haitians who lost their temporary status. Despite the legal victory, the lack of visible enforcement raids targeting this population has frustrated some of the president's most fervent backers.
articles.author: Madeleine Ngo and Hamed Aleaziz

articles.title: Trump informs Lisa Cook that he is “considering” her removal
articles.summary: President Trump has renewed his attempt to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, sending her a letter stating he is "considering" her removal and giving her 21 days to respond. The Supreme Court had temporarily blocked Trump's initial effort to fire Cook on June 29, stressing the importance of the Federal Reserve's independence from political influence.
articles.author: Amy Howe

articles.title: Trump signs new birthright citizenship order, ballroom dispute likely headed to Supreme Court
articles.summary: President Trump signed a new executive order narrowing birthright citizenship, just over a month after the Supreme Court struck down a broader earlier order on the same topic. The new order is expected to face legal challenges that will likely reach the Supreme Court again, and a separate dispute over a ballroom construction project is also headed to the high court.
articles.author: Amy Howe

articles.title: The Supreme Court of Japan
articles.summary: SCOTUSblog published an installment of its recurring series comparing supreme courts around the world, this time focusing on Japan's Supreme Court. The article, featuring Professor David S. Law, discusses the establishment, structure, and conservative reputation of Japan's highest court, drawing comparisons with the U.S. Supreme Court.
articles.author: Zachary Shemtob

articles.title: Pete Buttigieg, the Supreme Court, and the Fourth Amendment
articles.summary: An opinion piece discusses presidential candidate Pete Buttigieg's personal encounter with police and a Child Protective Services investigator at his home, using it as a lens to examine Fourth Amendment issues before the Supreme Court. The article explores the constitutional implications of law enforcement interactions at private residences.
articles.author: Jordan Lorence

articles.title: President Trump issues new birthright citizenship and “birth tourism” orders
articles.summary: This article covers President Trump's new executive orders on birthright citizenship and "birth tourism," issued after the Supreme Court struck down earlier restrictions. It also touches on a First Amendment issue related to license plates, described as the next major battleground for the court.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Nora Collins

articles.title: Trump says he’ll bring ballroom fight to Supreme Court after lower court halts work
articles.summary: An appeals court halted construction on a ballroom project that is among President Trump's top priorities, ruling that work must stop until Congress authorizes it. Trump has vowed to bring the dispute to the Supreme Court for resolution.
articles.author: Dan Diamond, Jonathan Edwards

articles.title: Trump won’t let the Supreme Court have the last word
articles.summary: President Trump moved this week to counter Supreme Court setbacks on multiple fronts, including issuing a new birthright citizenship order after the Court struck down the first one and renewing efforts to fire Fed Governor Lisa Cook after the Court temporarily blocked her removal. He is also seeking the Supreme Court's intervention in a ballroom construction dispute.
articles.author: Isaac Arnsdorf

articles.title: What is “trapped in amber”? An originalist explanation
articles.summary: The article examines the frequent use of the phrase "trapped in amber" in recent Supreme Court opinions, exploring its originalist significance. It references multiple cases from the past term, including Trump v. Cook and Watson v. Republican National Committee, where justices debated whether constitutional or statutory meanings should remain fixed or evolve over time.
articles.author: Haley Proctor

articles.title: Beyond the swing justice: majority makers, dissent bridges, and coalition drift on the Supreme Court
articles.summary: The article analyzes shifting coalition dynamics on the Supreme Court, noting Justice Amy Coney Barrett's rejection of the "swing justice" label in favor of being seen as independent. It examines how the traditional concept of a single swing justice has given way to more complex patterns of majority-building, dissent-bridging, and ideological drift among the current justices.
articles.author: Adam Feldman

articles.title: Tariff refunds reach $100 billion mark
articles.summary: The article reports that tariff refunds have reached the $100 billion mark and notes that a judge confirmed the end of Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Haitians. The piece appears to cover broader legal and policy developments rather than a specific Supreme Court case.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas

articles.title: Trump tries new tack against birthright citizenship after Supreme Court snub
articles.summary: President Trump signed new executive orders targeting birthright citizenship for children born to "alien enemies," foreign lobbyists, or tourists, after the Supreme Court rejected his earlier attempts to end birthright citizenship. The orders are expected to face immediate legal challenges, representing a revised strategy following the Court's rebuff.
articles.author: Isaac Arnsdorf, Justin Jouvenal, David Nakamura

articles.title: The justices should hold regular press conferences
articles.summary: The article argues that Supreme Court justices should hold regular press conferences to improve transparency and public communication. It discusses the court's current limited relationship with the press, including hard passes for journalists, occasional press releases, and the chief justice's annual year-end report. The piece is part of a series on reforms the author believes the court should adopt.
articles.author: Josh Blackman

articles.title: What does the Trump administration want from the Supreme Court next?
articles.summary: The Trump administration and President Trump's personal legal team have asked the Supreme Court to review an $83.3 million defamation judgment won by journalist E. Jean Carroll against Trump. The federal government's petition argues that Trump was acting in his official capacity as president when he made the statements about Carroll, and therefore should be entitled to immunity. The article examines what other cases or legal issues the administration may bring before the court next.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas

articles.title: The October argument session
articles.summary: The article previews the Supreme Court's October argument session and explains the historical reason the court's term begins on the first Monday in October. It provides an overview of the upcoming cases and oral arguments scheduled for the start of the new term.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Amy Howe

articles.title: Court announces cases it will hear in October, which include significant disputes on climate change and immigration detention
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has released its October 2026 argument calendar, with a major climate change lawsuit (Suncor Energy v. Commissioners of Boulder County) set as the first case of the new term. The session will also include significant disputes on immigration detention among other cases.
articles.author: Amy Howe

articles.title: Reproductive technologies and the federal constitutional vacuum
articles.summary: An adapted essay discusses the lack of Supreme Court guidance on constitutional questions surrounding reproductive technologies, including embryo destruction and surrogacy. The piece argues that while revolutionary new reproductive technologies are emerging, the Court has remained silent on the constitutional implications of technologies dating back decades.
articles.author: I. Glenn Cohen

articles.title: When the court denies racism that others see
articles.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that the Trump administration could proceed with ending humanitarian immigration protections (such as TPS) for hundreds of thousands of residents, finding that top officials did not racially discriminate against Haitians. Critics argue the majority applied an overly narrow definition of what constitutes racial language, denying racism that others clearly perceive in the administration's descriptions.
articles.author: César Cuauhtémoc García Hernández

articles.title: Why timing matters in the mail-in voting dispute
articles.summary: This piece discusses the significance of timing in a legal dispute over mail-in voting procedures, alongside a historical look at what happened to Dred Scott after his famous Supreme Court loss. The article highlights how procedural timing can shape the outcome of election-related cases before the Court.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Blake Fox

articles.title: States challenging executive order on mail-in voting ask justices to leave in place limits on its implementation
articles.summary: Twenty-three states and the District of Columbia are asking the Supreme Court to uphold a federal court order that blocks the government from enforcing an executive order on mail-in voting in their states ahead of November elections. The challengers argue that allowing the executive order to proceed would be legally indefensible and unprecedented.
articles.author: Amy Howe

articles.title: Born free and equal
articles.summary: A new SCOTUSblog columnist introduces their column "Born Free and Equal," explaining that the title derives from the Declaration of Independence on the occasion of its 250th anniversary. The article reflects on the foundational American constitutional principle that all people are created equal.
articles.author: Steven Gow Calabresi

articles.title: A court trapped in amber
articles.summary: The article examines how the Supreme Court's metaphor from United States v. Rahimi — that the Second Amendment is not "a law trapped in amber" — has become widely influential, appearing in six Supreme Court cases this term and hundreds of lower court opinions. The piece explores the irony that a phrase with roots in 1970s liberal thought has gained currency at a historically conservative court, while noting the metaphor defines what the law is not rather than what it is.
articles.author: Richard Re

articles.title: Trump administration targets birth tourism
articles.summary: The Trump administration is taking action to target birth tourism, while separately another prominent Democratic politician has come out in favor of expanding the Supreme Court. The article touches on both executive branch immigration policy and ongoing political debates about court reform.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Nora Collins

articles.title: The court and the “opinions of mankind”
articles.summary: This article reflects on the Declaration of Independence's 250th anniversary and its appeal to global opinion, arguing that the Supreme Court and the broader U.S. government have moved away from showing 'decent respect' to international perspectives. It discusses how current policies on tariffs, Iran, and other issues reflect a disregard for world opinion.
articles.author: Martin Flaherty

articles.title: The court’s big gun cases – and what’s next
articles.summary: The article reviews the Supreme Court's two major Second Amendment cases decided during the term: United States v. Hemani and Wolford v. Lopez. It notes this is the first time since District of Columbia v. Heller that the court decided more than one Second Amendment case in a single term, and reflects on their impact on gun rights jurisprudence.
articles.author: Alex Rivenbark

articles.title: Palestinian authorities seek Supreme Court relief
articles.summary: Palestinian authorities are seeking relief from the Supreme Court, though details are limited in the article's description. The article also examines whether Justice Kavanaugh has become the most prolific concurrence writer on the Roberts Court.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Nora Collins

articles.title: Completing the picture of the court’s criminal law term
articles.summary: This article provides a comprehensive listing of criminal law and related cases decided by the Supreme Court during the current term. It catalogs 19 merits cases and six summary dispositions broadly related to criminal law, offering court observers a complete picture of the Court's criminal law docket for the term.
articles.author: Rory Little

articles.title: How a seemingly unexciting case on retirement plans could have massive consequences
articles.summary: The article examines Anderson v. Intel Corporation Investment Policy Committee, a case about what allegations a lawsuit over retirement plans must include to survive initial legal challenges. Though the case may seem dry, it could have massive consequences for the more than 100 million Americans who save for retirement through employer-sponsored plans governed by federal law.
articles.author: Cory L. Andrews

articles.title: Justice Kavanaugh: the great concurrer of the Roberts court?
articles.summary: This opinion piece analyzes Justice Brett Kavanaugh's prolific use of concurring opinions, exploring whether he has become the 'great concurrer' of the Roberts Court. The article draws a historical comparison to Justice William Brennan's influential role on the Warren Court and examines Kavanaugh's strategic approach to shaping the law through separate writings.
articles.author: Rodger Citron

articles.title: Trump indicates that he will bring Hillary Clinton case to SCOTUS
articles.summary: Former President Trump has signaled his intention to bring a case involving Hillary Clinton to the Supreme Court. The article also covers petitions for certiorari related to an $83.3 million defamation verdict against the president.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas

articles.title: Trump asks Supreme Court to hear appeal of $83.3 million defamation verdict against him
articles.summary: President Trump's lawyers and the federal government have asked the Supreme Court to review the $83.3 million defamation verdict won by journalist E. Jean Carroll. A federal appeals court in New York had upheld the jury's award, and Trump's team argues the ruling improperly undermines presidential immunity. This would be a new case for the Court's docket if accepted.
articles.author: Amy Howe

articles.title: The push to reduce the Supreme Court’s power
articles.summary: Following a contentious Supreme Court term that included rulings on presidential removal power, the Voting Rights Act, and campaign finance regulations, some Democrats are pushing for structural reforms to the Court. Proposals include expanding the number of justices or imposing term limits to address what critics see as an entrenched conservative supermajority. The article examines the broader debate over reducing the Supreme Court's power.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas

articles.title: Gorsuch says Americans must study history, ‘warts, glories, and all’
articles.summary: Justice Neil Gorsuch spoke at a virtual forum where he described American democracy as "very fragile" and cautioned against any person or group having too much power. He emphasized the importance of young people studying an honest and complete version of American history, including both its achievements and failures. Gorsuch linked the decline in civics education to broader challenges facing democratic governance.
articles.author: Mark Walsh

articles.title: Trump urges SCOTUS to overturn $83.3 million defamation verdict
articles.summary: This article covers President Trump's petition urging the Supreme Court to overturn the $83.3 million defamation verdict awarded to E. Jean Carroll, alongside reporting that the Court's public approval rating has reached a new low. Trump's legal team is invoking presidential immunity as grounds for the appeal. The piece combines coverage of the Carroll case with broader public sentiment toward the Court.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Amy Howe

articles.title: Michelle Obama and Justice Jackson Talk Work-Life Balance and Public Service
articles.summary: Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson appeared on former First Lady Michelle Obama's podcast for a conversation about work-life balance and public service. The discussion was described as a rare public meeting between two prominent and popular Black women in American public life. The appearance offered a personal look at Justice Jackson outside of her judicial role.
articles.author: Ann E. Marimow

articles.title: An Alaskan Pilot. A Six-Pack of Beer. An Important Supreme Court Precedent.
articles.summary: The article previews an upcoming Supreme Court case involving an Alaskan pilot and a six-pack of beer, which raises the question of whether the Court will extend to ordinary individuals the same legal protections it has traditionally afforded to corporations. The case could set an important precedent regarding equal treatment under the law. The specific case likely involves a challenge to federal agency authority in Alaska.
articles.author: James J. Sample

articles.title: Trump asks Supreme Court to overturn $83 million verdict in E. Jean Carroll case
articles.summary: President Trump's attorneys have asked the Supreme Court to overturn the $83 million defamation verdict in the E. Jean Carroll case, citing the Court's 2024 decision granting presidents broad immunity for official actions taken in office. Trump's legal team argues that this immunity doctrine shields him from liability in Carroll's defamation lawsuit. The petition sets up a potential major test of the scope of presidential immunity.
articles.author: Justin Jouvenal, Jeremy Roebuck

articles.title: Trump administration appears not to have asked Supreme Court to rehear birthright citizenship case
articles.summary: The Trump administration appears to have let the deadline pass without filing a petition for rehearing in Trump v. Barbara, the birthright citizenship case. The Supreme Court had ruled on June 30 that President Trump's executive order ending birthright citizenship was unconstitutional, and the July 27 deadline for seeking reconsideration has now expired with no filing on the court's docket.
articles.author: Amy Howe

articles.title: Eliminate the summer recess
articles.summary: An opinion contributor to SCOTUSblog argues that the Supreme Court should eliminate its traditional summer recess as a form of unilateral institutional reform. The piece is part of a series exploring what the court can do on its own to improve its operations, without requiring congressional action.
articles.author: Josh Blackman

articles.title: Notable concurring opinions from this term
articles.summary: The article examines notable concurring opinions from the Supreme Court's most recent term, highlighting instances where justices used concurrences to advocate for significant changes in the law. It references Justice Clarence Thomas's concurrence in Mullin v. Doe, in which he argued that the equal protection clause does not apply to the federal government and that the landmark 1954 decision Bolling v. Sharpe was wrongly decided.
articles.author: Erwin Chemerinsky

articles.title: The ongoing battle over TPS status
articles.summary: This article discusses the ongoing legal battles over Temporary Protected Status (TPS) and also touches on how predictable Supreme Court outcomes are based on oral arguments. It appears to cover immigration policy disputes related to TPS designations currently before or recently addressed by the court.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Blake Fox

articles.title: Trump Asks Supreme Court to Overturn $83.3 Million Award in Carroll Defamation Case
articles.summary: President Trump has asked the Supreme Court to overturn an $83.3 million jury award from a 2024 defamation case brought by E. Jean Carroll. Trump had previously paid Carroll over $5 million from a separate 2023 lawsuit but is now seeking the high court's intervention to reverse the much larger damages award.
articles.author: Abbie VanSickle

articles.title: Trump administration asks Supreme Court to clear the way for new mail-in voting restrictions
articles.summary: The Trump administration asked the Supreme Court to allow full implementation of an executive order imposing new restrictions on mail-in voting. Solicitor General Sauer argued that a federal judge's order pausing parts of the executive order in 23 states and D.C. was extraordinary and violated legal doctrines about when courts can intervene.
articles.author: Amy Howe

articles.title: Why the Supreme Court decided the wrong issue in the transgender athletes cases
articles.summary: An opinion piece argues that the Supreme Court decided the wrong issue in West Virginia v. B.P.J., a case about transgender athletes. The Court held that state bans preventing transgender girls from participating in girls' sports violated neither Title IX nor the equal protection clause, but the author contends the Court should have focused on a different legal question.
articles.author: Craig Konnoth

articles.title: Justices’ lucrative book deals deserve more scrutiny
articles.summary: An outside opinion piece argues that Supreme Court justices' book deals deserve greater scrutiny, noting that justices have collectively earned over $10 million from book earnings. The piece highlights tensions between justices' statutory salaries and supplemental income from publishing deals under existing ethics rules.
articles.author: Gabe Roth

articles.title: How predictable is the Supreme Court from oral argument?
articles.summary: An analysis examines how predictable Supreme Court outcomes are based on oral arguments. The article uses Louisiana v. Callais as an example, noting that questioning from conservative justices during re-argument signaled the Court's eventual decision to curtail a major provision of the Voting Rights Act related to race-conscious redistricting.
articles.author: Adam Feldman

articles.title: Announcing The SCOTUSblog Summit: 2026 Term Preview
articles.summary: SCOTUSblog and Johns Hopkins University announced the SCOTUSblog Summit: 2026 Term Preview, scheduled for September 16 in Washington, D.C. The event will feature legal analysis panels, a live podcast recording, and discussions about the upcoming Supreme Court term with prominent general counsels and legal experts.
articles.author: SCOTUSblog Staff

articles.title: New tariffs, new lawsuits
articles.summary: A brief article discusses new lawsuits arising from recently imposed tariffs and promotes the upcoming 2026 SCOTUSblog Summit. The piece appears to touch on trade-related legal challenges that could potentially reach the Supreme Court.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas

articles.title: Trump Asks Supreme Court to Allow Order Restricting Mail Voting
articles.summary: The Trump administration asked the Supreme Court to intervene and allow enforcement of an executive order restricting mail-in voting after an appeals court blocked key parts of it. The case raises questions about executive authority over voting procedures and the scope of judicial power to block presidential orders.
articles.author: Abbie VanSickle

articles.title: The Constitutional Court of South Africa
articles.summary: SCOTUSblog published an installment of its series comparing supreme courts worldwide, this time focusing on the Constitutional Court of South Africa. The piece, featuring Professor Penelope Andrews, covers the court's establishment in 1994 and its structure. The article does not discuss any current U.S. Supreme Court case.
articles.author: Zachary Shemtob

articles.title: Is Elena Kagan the stare decisis justice?
articles.summary: An analysis piece examines Justice Elena Kagan's approach to stare decisis, highlighting her pride in her 2015 opinion in Kimble v. Marvel Entertainment, LLC, which upheld the precedent set by Brulotte v. Thys Co. The article explores Kagan's judicial philosophy regarding when the Supreme Court should and should not overrule its prior decisions. No current 2025-term SCOTUS case is directly discussed.
articles.author: Amy Howe

articles.title: Justice Kagan says court gets a "bad rap”
articles.summary: Justice Kagan publicly stated that the Supreme Court gets a "bad rap," and the piece also teases the question of whether the Court will take up a challenge to the federal ban on home distilling. The article touches on the Court's public perception and its upcoming case selection decisions.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Nora Collins

articles.title: Nine justices, nine styles
articles.summary: An outside contributor to SCOTUSblog analyzes the questioning styles of all nine Supreme Court justices during the October Term 2025 oral arguments. The study counted 5,095 questions across 58 oral arguments and examined patterns in how each justice approaches questioning. The piece explores whether advocates can predict the types of questions particular justices will ask.
articles.author: John Greil

articles.title: Dissents on the emergency docket are not created equal
articles.summary: A SCOTUSblog analysis examines dissents on the Supreme Court's emergency (shadow) docket, arguing that not all dissents carry the same weight or significance. The piece builds on prior reporting about the emergency docket's speed, secrecy, frequency of use, citation by lower courts, and justice shopping through refiled applications. It offers a new framework for understanding disagreements among the justices on emergency orders.
articles.author: Taraleigh Davis

articles.title: Democrats push Supreme Court term limits
articles.summary: Democratic lawmakers are pushing legislation to impose term limits on Supreme Court justices. The article also notes that the Court's policy regarding prediction markets is facing increased scrutiny.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Nora Collins

articles.title: Kagan Says Supreme Court Has Stood Up to Trump in Key Cases
articles.summary: Justice Elena Kagan, speaking at an annual gathering of judges and lawyers, defended her conservative colleagues on the Supreme Court against accusations that they have simply rubber-stamped President Trump's agenda. Kagan argued that the Court has stood up to the administration in key cases, pushing back on the narrative that the conservative majority is deferential to executive overreach.
articles.author: Abbie VanSickle

articles.title: Supreme Court Turbocharges Presidential Power
articles.summary: The Supreme Court issued a pair of decisions that significantly expanded presidential power, reshaping the structure of the federal government. The rulings represent a major shift in the balance of authority between the executive branch and other parts of the government.
articles.author: Adam Liptak

articles.title: Trump’s petition for reconsideration of $5 million verdict in E. Jean Carroll case may be considered by the justices in August
articles.summary: President Trump's petition asking the Supreme Court to reconsider its decision leaving in place the $5 million jury verdict in E. Jean Carroll's civil suit has been distributed to the justices. The Court could act on Trump's request as early as its next set of summer orders scheduled for August 17. The case stems from a 2023 federal jury verdict against Trump for sexual abuse and defamation.
articles.author: Amy Howe

articles.title: The case for Callais
articles.summary: An SCOTUSblog columnist offers a defense of the Supreme Court's 6-3 decision in Louisiana v. Callais, noting that the publication had previously only featured academic criticism of the ruling. The author argues Justice Scalia would have approved of the decision and questions why no other legal commentators have been willing to defend it.
articles.author: Brian Fitzpatrick

articles.title: The live blog comments that stuck with us
articles.summary: SCOTUSblog reflects on memorable reader comments and questions from its live blog coverage of major oral arguments and opinion release days. The piece highlights the popular interactive feature and acknowledges the recurring reader curiosity about when particular opinions will be released.
articles.author: Nora Collins

articles.title: Judicial ethics in the spotlight
articles.summary: SCOTUSblog covers developments related to judicial ethics at the Supreme Court, alongside news about the Trump administration's efforts to rebuild its tariff regime. The article appears to touch on broader issues of court transparency and ethical standards for justices.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Amy Howe

articles.title: The history the court would rather not see
articles.summary: The article examines the Supreme Court's history-and-tradition test established in the 2021 Bruen decision for evaluating Second Amendment challenges to gun laws. It raises questions about the methodology of finding historical analogs to justify modern firearm regulations and explores historical evidence that the court may be reluctant to consider.
articles.author: Daniel Harawa

articles.title: Heller and Bruen are here to stay
articles.summary: The article reviews the Supreme Court's October 2025 term as a strong one for Second Amendment rights. In United States v. Hemani, the court unanimously ruled that disarming someone solely for occasional marijuana use violates the Second Amendment, and in Wolford v. Lopez, the court struck down Hawaii's presumptive ban on carrying firearms in establishments open to the public.
articles.author: Pete Patterson

articles.title: The ripple effects of the TPS ruling
articles.summary: The article discusses the broader implications of the Supreme Court's ruling on Temporary Protected Status (TPS). It also notes that the justices added a new case involving a seized plane and a six-pack of beer to next term's oral argument docket.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Nora Collins

articles.title: Democrats Still Knock the Supreme Court, Even When It Checks Trump
articles.summary: House Democrats are renewing efforts to impose term limits on Supreme Court justices and expand the number of seats on the court. The push continues even as the court has issued rulings that check presidential power under the Trump administration.
articles.author: Charles Hilu

articles.title: Supreme Court agrees to hear case on whether airplane was improperly seized for transporting a six-pack of beer
articles.summary: The Supreme Court agreed to hear Jouppi v. Alaska, a case involving an Alaskan bush pilot who challenges the forfeiture of his $95,000 airplane. Prosecutors sought the forfeiture because a passenger brought a six-pack of beer into a village where alcohol is prohibited, and the pilot argues the seizure was improper. The case has been added to the oral argument docket for the 2026-27 term.
articles.author: Amy Howe

articles.title: When it comes to getting the Supreme Court’s attention, does one state have an edge?
articles.summary: A SCOTUSblog analysis found that Texas had the most individual litigants in cases argued before the Supreme Court during the 2025-26 term, with five disputes involving Texans. The article highlights Ali Danial Hemani's victory in United States v. Hemani as one example. The analysis examined 35 argued cases that had a single person or family on one side of the case.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas

articles.title: Almost half of Americans view SCOTUS as political
articles.summary: A recent survey found that almost half of Americans view the Supreme Court as a political institution. The article also notes that the Trump administration's ban on transgender troops is likely to return to the Supreme Court for further review.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Nora Collins

articles.title: Johnny Brown, Justice Jackson’s father, passes away at 80
articles.summary: Johnny Brown, the father of Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson, has passed away at age 80. Justice Jackson's visit to the University of Alaska Fairbanks was cut short due to the personal emergency. The news was confirmed through an obituary published in the Miami Herald.
articles.author: Amy Howe

articles.title: In birthright citizenship dissent, Justice Thomas stakes out an ideological claim of who counts as an American
articles.summary: The Supreme Court ruled against President Trump's executive order attempting to narrow birthright citizenship, with a majority finding it illegal. Justices Thomas and Gorsuch dissented, framing the case as an ideological question about who counts as an American rather than a straightforward 14th Amendment textual analysis. The long-awaited decision in Trump v. Barbara blocked the federal government from restricting birthright citizenship.
articles.author: César Cuauhtémoc García Hernández

articles.title: Three profound constitutional provisions – and how the Supreme Court has avoided dealing with them
articles.summary: An analysis piece discusses three constitutional provisions that the Supreme Court has largely avoided addressing: the 13th Amendment's exception clause, Article IV's guarantee clause, and the Third Amendment. Despite their profound implications, these provisions rarely come before the Court compared to more frequently litigated amendments like the First, Second, and Fourth. The article explores why these clauses have flown under the Court's radar.
articles.author: Nora Collins

articles.title: Rebecca Slaughter speaks out
articles.summary: Rebecca Slaughter, an FTC commissioner involved in a Supreme Court case about presidential removal power, has spoken publicly. The brief piece also directs readers to recent SCOTUSblog event videos for additional coverage of Supreme Court developments.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Nora Collins

articles.title: The administrative agency cases were not the court’s only significant separation of powers decisions this term
articles.summary: An analysis piece discusses the Supreme Court's separation of powers decisions this term, highlighting not only the well-known administrative agency cases Trump v. Slaughter and Trump v. Cook, but also the less-noticed decisions in Rutherford v. United States and Fernandez v. United States, which also addressed the relationship between branches of government.
articles.author: Kevin Trowel

articles.title: The public’s view of the Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Marquette Law School Poll examines how closely public opinion aligns with Supreme Court decisions. The article discusses polling data tracking public approval of the court and the public's views on outcomes of pending cases throughout the term.
articles.author: Charles Franklin

articles.title: Reactions to Kagan and Barrett’s congressional testimony
articles.summary: The article covers reactions to congressional testimony by Justices Kagan and Barrett, and also notes the Trump administration's filing of a new petition for Supreme Court review related to Temporary Protected Status.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas

articles.title: Trump administration asks justices to have lower court reconsider protected status for Venezuelan and Haitian nationals
articles.summary: The Trump administration's Solicitor General asked the Supreme Court to send a case back to the 9th Circuit for reconsideration, involving the termination of Temporary Protected Status for Venezuelan and Haitian nationals by then-DHS Secretary Kristi Noem. The case concerns whether foreign nationals can remain and work in the U.S. when they cannot safely return to their home countries.
articles.author: Amy Howe

articles.title: Narrow holdings with broad consequences
articles.summary: The article analyzes two Second Amendment decisions from the Supreme Court's latest term. In United States v. Hemani, the court unanimously struck down a federal law criminalizing firearm possession by unlawful drug users, and in Wolford v. Lopez, the court invalidated a Hawaii concealed-carry law requiring express property owner permission to carry on private property open to the public.
articles.author: Haley Proctor

articles.title: The court’s criminal law term: overview and observations
articles.summary: This article provides an overview of the Supreme Court's criminal law decisions from the October 2025-26 term, noting that 16 of the 57 argued cases (28%) were "pure" criminal law cases. It also references First Choice v. Davenport, a civil case with standing implications, as potentially raising the count to 17.
articles.author: Rory Little

articles.title: Carroll receives payment from Trump
articles.summary: The article reports that E. Jean Carroll has received payment from Donald Trump, likely related to prior defamation litigation. It also notes that Justices Kagan and Barrett spoke to Congress about security concerns facing the Supreme Court.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Amy Howe

articles.title: Justices Kagan and Barrett testify before Congress
articles.summary: Justices Elena Kagan and Amy Coney Barrett testified before both chambers of Congress, marking the first such appearances by Supreme Court justices in seven years. While the primary focus was the court's budget, they also discussed security, enforcement of the court's ethics code, and the emergency/interim docket.
articles.author: Amy Howe

articles.title: Two cheers – but not three – for Roberts and Barrett
articles.summary: The article praises Chief Justice Roberts and Justice Barrett for their decisive roles in two major end-of-term cases. In Trump v. Barbara, they joined the three liberal justices to form a 5-member majority affirming that the 14th Amendment's equal protection clause guarantees birthright citizenship, while the other four justices dissented.
articles.author: Edward Foley

articles.title: The biggest Supreme Court surprises this term
articles.summary: The article discusses the biggest surprises from the Supreme Court's latest term, noting that while outcomes in major cases on tariffs, presidential removal power, birthright citizenship, and transgender athlete restrictions were largely predictable from oral arguments, the birthright citizenship decision's specific reasoning was unexpected. The author reflects on the limits of prediction even for experienced court watchers.
articles.author: Erwin Chemerinsky

articles.title: Executive Power and its Limits
articles.summary: This is a transcript of a discussion about executive power and its limits in the context of the Supreme Court's recent term. The conversation explores the boundaries of presidential authority as shaped by the court's latest rulings.
articles.author: SCOTUSblog Staff

articles.title: A history of justices testifying before Congress
articles.summary: The article provides historical context for Supreme Court justices testifying before Congress, ahead of Justices Kagan and Barrett appearing before House and Senate subcommittees to discuss the court's budget request. It notes this is a rare occurrence in the court's history.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Nora Collins

articles.title: The Supreme Court and the opinion-assignment guessing game
articles.summary: The article examines the long-standing practice among Supreme Court watchers of trying to guess which justice is writing which remaining opinion based on the court's internal convention of distributing opinions roughly equally across argument sittings. By tracking how many opinions each justice has released from each monthly sitting, observers attempt to deduce who holds the outstanding decisions. The piece explores how reliable this guessing game actually is and what it reveals about the court's workflow.
articles.author: Adam Feldman

articles.title: A dissent worthy of a World Cup
articles.summary: The article draws a connection between the upcoming World Cup final at MetLife Stadium and a historic Supreme Court case involving the North American Soccer League's antitrust challenge against the NFL. The NASL accused the NFL of anticompetitive practices through rules that barred team owners from owning franchises in rival leagues. The piece revisits the case and highlights a notable dissent from that era in light of soccer's now-thriving presence in America.
articles.author: Anastasia Boden

articles.title: How Justice Samuel Alito stands out
articles.summary: The article analyzes Justice Samuel Alito's distinctive patterns and positions on the Supreme Court, examining how he stands out among his colleagues. It also takes a closer look at the court's summer order lists, which handle pending petitions and other business during the recess period.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Nora Collins

articles.title: With Threats Rising, Supreme Court Asks Congress to Increase Security Funds
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has asked Congress for more than $200 million in security funding amid rising threats against the justices. Justices Amy Coney Barrett and Elena Kagan are scheduled to make a rare joint appearance before Congress to testify in support of the budget request. The appeal underscores growing concerns about the safety of Supreme Court justices in the current political climate.
articles.author: Ann E. Marimow

articles.title: The limits of the Second Amendment
articles.summary: This article explores unresolved questions about the Second Amendment's scope, following up on previous discussions about who qualifies as 'the people' and what counts as 'Arms.' It examines the limits of Second Amendment protections as outlined by the Supreme Court in District of Columbia v. Heller and subsequent cases.
articles.author: Alex Rivenbark

articles.title: The man and the movement: a Q&A with Peter Canellos on his biography of Samuel Alito
articles.summary: SCOTUSblog features a Q&A with journalist Peter Canellos about his biography of Justice Samuel Alito, titled 'Revenge for the Sixties.' The book examines Alito's role in the conservative legal movement and how his decisions have reshaped American law through his tenure on the Supreme Court.
articles.author: Ronald Collins

articles.title: High court mysteries
articles.summary: This article examines the many mysteries and opaque practices of the Supreme Court, noting that despite justices being more publicly visible than ever—with six having published books and several giving interviews—the institution itself remains far from transparent. It explores various customs, practices, and unexplained events at the Court.
articles.author: Stephen Wermiel

articles.title: The rarity of Supreme Court do-overs
articles.summary: This article discusses the rarity of the Supreme Court revisiting or redoing its decisions, and also highlights comments from attorney Cecillia Wang about arguing the birthright citizenship case during SCOTUSblog's term-in-review event. The birthright citizenship case relates to challenges against the Trump administration's executive actions.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Nora Collins

articles.title: This Is a Lot More Worrying Than the Supreme Court’s Ruling on Executive Power
articles.summary: This New York Times opinion piece argues that while the Supreme Court's recent ruling on executive power has drawn attention, the more concerning development is the White House bypassing Congress to make significant decisions affecting major private industries. The article focuses on the broader implications of executive overreach beyond the Court's specific ruling.
articles.author: David Lawrence

articles.title: At SCOTUSblog’s term-in-review event, National Legal Director of the ACLU Cecillia Wang speaks about arguing birthright citizenship, the term in general, and what’s next on the organization’s docket
articles.summary: ACLU National Legal Director Cecillia Wang discussed her experience arguing the birthright citizenship case, Trump v. Barbara, before the Supreme Court, describing it as the most high-stakes moment of her career. She spoke at SCOTUSblog's term-in-review event about the case, the overall term, and the ACLU's future legal priorities.
articles.author: Amy Howe

articles.title: Justice shopping on the emergency docket?
articles.summary: The article examines the practice of refiling emergency applications with different justices on the Supreme Court's emergency docket, a lesser-known procedural maneuver sometimes called "justice shopping." It explores how litigants may strategically refile applications after an initial denial, raising questions about the process's transparency and fairness.
articles.author: Taraleigh Davis

articles.title: Who is the Supreme Court’s most “ideological” justice? And does that question even make sense?
articles.summary: The article analyzes whether it is meaningful to label individual Supreme Court justices as the most "ideological," examining the familiar grouping of the court into conservative, liberal, and moderate blocs. It questions whether the conventional shorthand of placing justices on a simple left-right spectrum accurately captures the complexity of their judicial philosophies and voting patterns.
articles.author: Adam Feldman

articles.title: Trump wants court to rehear birthright citizenship case
articles.summary: The Trump administration announced it wants the Supreme Court to rehear the birthright citizenship case, Trump v. Barbara, an extraordinarily rare procedural request. The article also provides a brief overview of SCOTUSblog's term-in-review event covering the recently concluded term.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas

articles.title: How the Supreme Court’s Conservative Supermajority Is Reshaping Executive Power
articles.summary: The article examines how the Supreme Court's conservative supermajority shaped executive power during the most recent term, largely siding with or declining to check President Trump's assertions of authority. Those who hoped the judiciary would serve as a meaningful counterweight to executive overreach were mostly disappointed by the term's outcomes.

articles.title: Trump Says He’ll Ask Supreme Court to Rehear Citizenship Case, an Unlikely Event
articles.summary: President Trump announced he will ask the Supreme Court to rehear the birthright citizenship case, an event that would be virtually unprecedented in modern history. The last time the Court granted a rehearing petition after deciding a case was in 1965, and the Court has only once reversed itself on rehearing.
articles.author: Erica L. Green and Abbie VanSickle

articles.title: SCOTUS Vibe Check
articles.summary: The article provides an overall review and assessment of the Supreme Court's October Term 2025, offering a broad "vibe check" on the justices' work and the term's major themes. It surveys the tone and direction of the Court's decisions across the recently concluded term.
articles.author: Sarah Isgur, David French

articles.title: Revisiting which Supreme Court cases are actually the most important
articles.summary: An outside opinion piece on SCOTUSblog revisits a method of measuring the importance of Supreme Court cases by counting the number of amicus curiae briefs filed in each case. The author argues that the volume of friend-of-the-court briefs serves as a market-like signal of a case's significance, since filing requires meaningful investment of time, money, and reputation.
articles.author: Eric McKee

articles.title: The Supreme Court’s quiet coup
articles.summary: An outside opinion piece argues that the Roberts Supreme Court is engaged in a systematic transfer of power away from Congress and toward the presidency. The author contends that while the expansion of presidential power is highly visible, the Court's erosion of congressional authority is a less obvious but equally significant shift in the balance of governmental power.
articles.author: Christopher A. Coons, David Beier, Ray Brescia

articles.title: Kagan and Barrett to testify before Congress
articles.summary: Justices Elena Kagan and Amy Coney Barrett are set to testify before Congress. Additionally, former President Trump has asked the Supreme Court to reconsider his appeal of a $5 million jury award, likely referring to the E. Jean Carroll defamation case.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Amy Howe

articles.title: The Supreme Court’s disturbing approach to federal spending
articles.summary: The article analyzes the Supreme Court's majority opinion in Landor v. Louisiana Department of Corrections, decided on June 23, arguing that the ruling treats federal spending programs in a troubling way. The author contends that the decision's premise—that federal spending programs should be subject to stricter scrutiny—has massive and disturbing implications for the future of government funding and policy.
articles.author: Erwin Chemerinsky

articles.title: Justice Jackson reignites the interpretation wars, adding to textualism’s emerging cracks
articles.summary: The article examines Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson's series of separate opinions this term protesting the majority's refusal to consult legislative history in statutory interpretation cases. It frames her efforts as the beginning of a potential revolution in statutory interpretation methodology, representing emerging cracks in the textualist approach that has dominated the Court for over a decade.
articles.author: Abbe R. Gluck

articles.title: Is Chief Justice Roberts moderating from the front?
articles.summary: The article discusses Chief Justice John Roberts's evolving role on the Supreme Court, pushing back against claims that he is purely a conservative ideologue rather than an institutionalist. It argues that Roberts has occupied three different institutional roles over the past eight years and that his approach to institutionalism has adapted to changing conditions on the Court.
articles.author: Richard Re

articles.title: The latest emergency docket ruling
articles.summary: This article covers the Supreme Court's latest ruling on its emergency docket and considers whether the justices will have a quiet summer following the conclusion of their argued cases for the term. It appears to be a brief overview of end-of-term activity on the shadow docket.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Nora Collins

articles.title: The Supreme Court Ruling That Further Politicizes Everyday Life
articles.summary: The article analyzes the Supreme Court's ruling in Trump v. Slaughter, arguing that the decision goes beyond expanding executive control and allows the government to exert partisan influence over more aspects of Americans' everyday lives. The piece frames the ruling as one that further politicizes ordinary aspects of daily life in the United States.
articles.author: David A. Graham

articles.title: Supreme Court justices to make rare appearance before Congress
articles.summary: Justices Elena Kagan and Amy Coney Barrett, representing the Court's liberal and conservative wings respectively, are scheduled to testify before a House subcommittee next Tuesday in a rare appearance by Supreme Court justices before Congress. The article highlights the unusual nature of sitting justices making such an appearance on Capitol Hill.
articles.author: Julian Mark

articles.title: Supreme Court allows Texas to enforce law requiring age verification and parental consent on apps
articles.summary: The Supreme Court allowed Texas to continue enforcing a law requiring app stores to verify users' ages and obtain parental consent before minors can download apps or make in-app purchases. The justices denied requests to reinstate a lower court's orders blocking the law, with no public dissents noted.
articles.author: Amy Howe

articles.title: The justices remained busy last summer. This year, will they actually get a break?
articles.summary: The article reflects on last year's busy summer at the Supreme Court, which included major rulings on universal injunctions and a state ban on medical treatments for transgender minors, and asks whether the justices will have a quieter recess this year. It notes that the court typically takes a break from petitions, arguments, and decisions during the summer.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas

articles.title: The powerful, resilient, independent Supreme Court
articles.summary: This opinion piece discusses the Supreme Court's institutional resilience and independence in the face of controversial actions by the Trump administration. It examines the court's role during what many observers described as a constitutional crisis, evaluating whether the justices adequately checked executive power.
articles.author: Jack Goldsmith

articles.title: Is the Roberts court hyperopic or willfully blind?
articles.summary: This opinion essay examines whether the Roberts Court is strategically farsighted or deliberately ignoring immediate concerns, noting an emerging theme in which the conservative side of the court typically prevails on issues of broader significance. The piece references observations made at a Federalist Society event about patterns in the court's recent term.
articles.author: Michael Dorf

articles.title: Looking back and looking ahead
articles.summary: The article provides a retrospective on the Supreme Court's just-completed term, describing it as momentous, and previews the upcoming term as potentially equally consequential. It serves as a bridge piece summarizing key developments and flagging cases to watch.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Nora Collins

articles.title: How Political Is This Supreme Court?
articles.summary: Legal commentator Elie Honig argues that the Trump-appointed Supreme Court justices are receiving unfair criticism for being overly political. The piece explores the broader debate about how politically motivated the current Supreme Court's decisions truly are.
articles.author: Isaac Chotiner

articles.title: Supreme Court Allows Texas Age-Verification Law for App Stores, for Now
articles.summary: The Supreme Court allowed Texas to enforce a law requiring Apple and Google to verify app store users' ages and obtain parental consent for minors, at least temporarily. The ruling keeps the Texas law in effect while legal challenges continue.
articles.author: Ann E. Marimow

articles.title: Justice Alito Gives No Indication He’s Ready to Step Down From the Supreme Court
articles.summary: Justice Samuel Alito showed no signs of retiring from the Supreme Court despite speculation, having authored significant conservative majority opinions this term on voting rights, immigration, and gun-related cases. The article discusses his influential role in shaping the Court's rightward direction and his apparent intent to remain on the bench.
articles.author: Abbie VanSickle and Ann E. Marimow

articles.title: A tale of two justices and their children’s books
articles.summary: The article takes a lighter look at the end of the Supreme Court's 2025-26 term, highlighting children's books written by justices. It focuses on Justice Neil Gorsuch's new book "Heroes of 1776," co-written with former law clerk Janie Nitze, and notes Justice Sonia Sotomayor has also written for young readers.
articles.author: Rodger Citron

articles.title: The Trump term?
articles.summary: The Supreme Court's 2025-26 term is being characterized as potentially the most consequential in recent memory, particularly for President Trump. Trump was a named party in four major cases and became the first sitting president to attend oral argument, but suffered high-profile losses on tariffs, birthright citizenship, and his attempt to remove Federal Reserve Board member Lisa Cook.
articles.author: Amy Howe

articles.title: 250 and the court
articles.summary: SCOTUSblog published an animated explainer summarizing key takeaways about the Supreme Court from the 2025-26 term, timed to coincide with the nation's 250th anniversary. The piece is a broad overview rather than a discussion of any specific case.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Nora Collins

articles.title: John Roberts, the US chief justice playing the long game
articles.summary: The Financial Times profiles Chief Justice John Roberts and his long-term strategic approach to leading the Supreme Court. The article highlights how, during the most recent term, Roberts steered the Court to defy President Trump on some issues while simultaneously expanding the scope of presidential power in other rulings.

articles.title: An immigration law error in the court’s asylum decision threatens immigration courts
articles.summary: The article critiques the Supreme Court's decision in Mullin v. Al Otro Lado, which blocked migrants stopped at the international boundary from applying for asylum. The author argues that the majority misunderstood the border-crossing process Congress created in federal immigration law, effectively giving border officers unchecked power to deny asylum access.
articles.author: César Cuauhtémoc García Hernández

articles.title: After Slaughter and Cook: future Fed fights, and maybe some midnight firings
articles.summary: The article examines the implications of the Supreme Court's decisions in Slaughter and Cook for the future of independent federal agencies. It discusses how these rulings affect presidential power to fire agency heads, potentially upending the longstanding Humphrey's Executor precedent that allowed Congress to shield agencies from total presidential control.
articles.author: Adam White

articles.title: What we learned about the court this term: an animated explainer
articles.summary: This animated explainer reviews the Supreme Court's 2025-26 term, analyzing which justices were most influential, key judicial alliances, and whether the court's ideological divide is overstated. It is the third in a series of animated videos produced in partnership with Briefly.
articles.author: SCOTUSblog Staff, Briefly

articles.title: The Stat Pack is back
articles.summary: The article announces the release of the "Stat Pack" for the Supreme Court's 2025-26 term, compiled by Jake S. Truscott and Adam Feldman. It presents statistical analysis and key takeaways from the term's decisions.
articles.author: Kelsey Dallas, Nora Collins

articles.title: Supreme Court Allows Reporter to Be Fined for Failing to Disclose Source
articles.summary: The Supreme Court allowed a lower court's civil contempt finding against former Fox News reporter Catherine Herridge to stand after she refused to reveal confidential sources for articles about an FBI investigation of a scientist. The decision has significant implications for press freedom and journalists' ability to protect their sources.
articles.author: Ann E. Marimow

articles.title: In Tumultuous Term, Chief Justice Roberts Took Charge of Unruly Supreme Court
articles.summary: The article profiles Chief Justice John Roberts's leadership during a tumultuous Supreme Court term, highlighting how he confronted the president, built unexpected coalitions among the justices, and advanced long-sought legal goals. It portrays Roberts as taking charge of a fractured court during a politically charged period.
articles.author: Adam Liptak

articles.title: What the Supreme Court Has Wrought
articles.summary: This opinion piece compiles reader perspectives on the Supreme Court's just-completed term, reflecting on the impact of its major rulings. Readers share diverse views on what the court's decisions mean for the country's legal and political landscape.

articles.title: The Supreme Court’s Slaughter Decision Is Only Half the Battle
articles.summary: The article argues that while the Supreme Court's Slaughter decision was significant, it represents only part of the challenge in constraining executive power. The author contends that Congress must also be compelled to fulfill its role in holding the executive branch accountable.
articles.author: Ryan J. Owens

articles.title: Three cheers for Barbara!
articles.summary: The article celebrates the Supreme Court's majority opinion in Trump v. Barbara, which struck down President Trump's executive order 14160 that sought to end birthright citizenship.
